subtitle: A living canvas for ecological time, rendered as light
thesis: The artwork is not the flower but what the flower does over a year. The core unsolved problem: what does a plant mean when it stops being a flower and becomes a pixel?

steps.title: The reframe
steps.question: Is GardenOS an 'AI garden visualiser'?
steps.decision: No — it is the experience of a garden through time. Spatial art vs temporal art. Render biological process as light, not image.
steps.learned: Named the one hard problem all later steps probe: what a plant means as a pixel.

steps.title: Trial 01 · Ecological Time
steps.question: Can temporal abstraction read as both beautiful and legible — can you tell species apart from behaviour alone?
steps.decision: Smallest probe. Each species is a verb, not a picture: tulip=colour field, allium=ring, foxglove=spire, hosta=shadow mass, poppy=ignition.
steps.learned: Establishes the interpretation vocabulary before any renderer work.

steps.title: Direction fork
steps.question: Push the thesis (non-garden dataset) or the beauty (shaders)? What is the end-form?
steps.decision: Chase the beauty. End-form = gallery / installation piece.
steps.learned: For an installation, presence and beauty ARE the product, so the shader is the correct next build — not a detour.

steps.title: Trial 03 · Living Canvas
steps.question: Does the idea survive the Rothko / LED quality it promises?
steps.decision: Ping-pong feedback buffer (light decays + diffuses = memory) + multi-tap bloom + ACES tonemap. CPU computes garden state, shader paints behaviours.
steps.learned: FINDING: bloom is drowning legibility — the allium ring dissolves into glow. The beauty-vs-readability tension appears on the first shader frame. Next: tune bloom / give each species a signature that survives it.

steps.title: Tune bloom · recover the allium ring
steps.question: Can structural behaviours survive the bloom that gives the piece its gallery quality?
steps.decision: Threshold the bloom (b = max(b-0.12,0)*1.25) so only the bright tail halos; tighter glow radius + 1/fr^2 falloff; bloom 1.15->0.62; added a hard ring-core term to allium; tightened feedback diffusion 1.4->0.9.
steps.learned: Beauty-vs-readability is resolvable, not a trade-off: bloom the bright tail, protect the cores. Reusable principle — every species gets a crisp core that bloom can halo but not erase. Side-effect: darker ground, higher contrast, tulip/hosta masses read better too.

steps.title: Pressure-test: have we taken shortcuts?
steps.question: Are we shipping something live rather than building the full advanced suite?
steps.decision: Yes, deliberately. Trials 01-03 keyframed the entire biology — a mood-board of output, not the system. The advanced move (GPGPU ecological substrate) IS the point of the project, so build it now. Wrote ARCHITECTURE.md as the 5-layer spec.
steps.learned: Three real ceilings (not deferred polish): no simulation, all hardcoded in one file, renderer capped at 16 entities.

steps.title: Trial 05 · Ecological Substrate (Layer 2 for real)
steps.tool: Three.js + GLSL GPGPU (ping-pong FBOs, half-float field)
steps.question: Can spread, competition, succession and multi-year change EMERGE from a GPU simulation instead of being keyframed?
steps.decision: Spatial Lotka-Volterra reaction-diffusion: RGBA field (3 species + shared resource), 512x288 ~147k cells, diffusion + competition + seasonal growth windows, timestep tied to days elapsed.
steps.learned: Proven, but failed twice instructively. Bug 1: isolated point-spores evaporate via diffusion (negative Laplacian >> growth) -> fix: smooth FBM seeding + day-clocked timestep. Bug 2: naive shared-resource model is STABILIZING -> homogenizes to a uniform wash by Year 2 -> fix: seasonal die-back clears the canvas + patchy year-drifting spore rain reseeds it (prevents both extinction and homogenization, gives Year2 != Year1). Knife-edge: too little death homogenizes, too much goes extinct; real ecology resolves it with a seed bank. Keyframing sidestepped the hardest, most interesting problem.

steps.title: Trial 06 · First-Person Garden (the camera change)
steps.tool: Three.js perspective scene (layered billboards + fog + threshold bloom)
steps.question: User: it doesn't look like a garden — make it first-person, looking out, with depth layers, growth coming up, green as background.
steps.decision: Wrong camera, not wrong idea. Perspective scene: 12 vegetation billboards receding into green fog (depth + 'green background'), per-column foliage silhouettes rising with a seasonal growth curve (growth coming up), blooms as colour events rising through foliage tops with per-season palettes (spring red/gold, summer violet/white, autumn ember). Carried threshold-bloom + ACES.
steps.learned: The project's legibility lived in the VIEWPOINT, not the simulation — the same seasonal idea reads as mush from above and as a garden from within. HONEST GAP: Trial 06 is driven by a season curve, NOT the Trial 05 substrate, so emergent spread/competition/succession are gone again. Got the camera right but dropped the ecology. Trial 07 must feed the substrate's species fields in as the planting map for this perspective renderer.

steps.title: Trial 06b · Garden Variants (aesthetic fork)
steps.question: Refine the first-person garden with a few variants to choose a look.
steps.decision: One file, four presets switchable live under identical geometry/season: Giverny (painterly warm), Nocturne (dark gallery/LED, blooms as light), Meadow (sunlit dense gold), Sumi (muted fog, sparse, negative space). Each drives fog/sky/ground/greens/bloom/palette/post.
steps.learned: Four clearly differentiated directions. Shared remaining flaw: blooms read as horizontal aurora-bands hugging the ridge, not discrete flowers; plus a foreground seam/streak artifact. Real fix = render blooms as point sprites / instanced flowers, deferred until a direction is chosen.

steps.title: Nocturne locked + blooms as points
steps.question: Make blooms read as discrete points of light, not aurora-bands.
steps.decision: Locked Nocturne. Replaced per-column bloom glow with ~1800 particle sprites tied to species season windows, rising and igniting in season, fog dissolving far ones.
steps.learned: Points are the right primitive but read faint against the bright foliage silhouette WALL — user named the deeper problem: plants are a 'square block', not individual plants.

steps.title: Brush Strokes — foliage as individual plants
steps.question: User: plants shouldn't be one square block — render individual plants, like brush strokes.
steps.decision: Removed the billboard silhouette walls. Foliage is now ~16k individual instanced strokes — tapered Y-billboarded brush marks rising from the ground, per-instance height/width/shade/species + 30% flowering. Flowering plants ignite an HDR tip in their season → post bloom makes points of light. Foliage and blooms both discrete instances.
steps.learned: Breakthrough for the look — reads unmistakably as individual plants receding to horizon; 16k strokes run fine. Remaining: reads as uniform MEADOW not a structured border — needs clumping (beds/drifts), more height variation / tall architectural plants, summer violet still pale.

steps.title: Plant Types — distinct foliage, clumping, tall plants
steps.tool: Three.js instanced strokes composed into archetypes (~22k)
steps.question: User: foliage should differ by plant (not one stroke x16k); think about clumping + tall plants.
steps.decision: Compose the garden from 5 plant ARCHETYPES, each a different arrangement of strokes with its own foliage colour/shape/flowering: grass (arching tuft), mound (broad blue-green hosta, foliage only), spire (tall, flowers up top), umbel (tall stem + bright ball), daisy (bushy heads). Planted in DRIFTS (clustered beds + gaussian spread) not even scatter; loose grass matrix between. Per-instance foliage colour/shape/bend/flower-window as attributes (no uniform-array indexing).
steps.learned: Archetypes + clumping turn the uniform meadow into a border with structure; tall spires/umbels above the low foliage give the 'layers / coming up' read the user wanted. Remaining: tall accents read as uniform 'light sticks' (vary thickness/curve); summer violet washes white; drifts could be stronger; still a season curve.

steps.title: Roundness — silhouette shapes
steps.tool: Three.js instanced strokes + per-instance silhouette shape
steps.question: User: everything looks like an agave plant — no roundness.
steps.decision: Every stroke now carries a silhouette shape (half-width profile): blade(pointed), leaf(ovate rounded), stem, ball(stem+round bloom head), bush(soft rounded), dome(low cushion). Rebalanced toward rounded forms + added cushion archetype; varied spire/umbel width+curve (no more light-sticks); tighter drifts; more saturated violet + gentler tip so it keeps colour.
steps.learned: Roundness lives in the silhouette profile; one iShape attribute unlocks the whole spiky<->round, tall<->low vocabulary within the same instanced system. Reads as mixed planting now. Remaining: a touch sparse/dark (tighter drifts left bare ground); violet still slightly pale at peak; still a season curve.

steps.title: Layers Through Time (six-layer model)
steps.tool: Three.js: dapple field + particle layers (pollinators, leaf-fall) + event ticker
steps.question: User design: garden = six ecological layers + four zones, simulated as events not plants, as a time machine.
steps.decision: Captured the model in MODEL.md. Built the layer that drives everything (CANOPY: drifting dappled shade sampled by ground+plants, leaf-on tied to season; autumn LEAF-FALL particles; canopy curtain overhead) + the POLLINATOR layer (~150 bee/hoverfly motes, erratic flight, amount tracks warm season) + an EVENT ticker in the HUD. On top of the 07d stroke garden.
steps.learned: The conceptual turn from 'a garden' to 'layers moving through time'. Dappled shade alone transforms the read (cool-lit foreground hosta = best frame yet); pollinators + leaf-fall give life + events. Needed a legibility pass (Nocturne + shade compounded to murk → lightened shade, lifted exposure, brightened leaves). Remaining: canopy silhouette felt not seen (overhead curtain too dark); still one zone on a season curve.

steps.title: Daytime Canopy (the garden is mostly leaves)
steps.tool: Three.js: ~40k leaf-dab instances clustered into foliage masses + branches + petal particles
steps.question: User (with garden photo): need DAYTIME; more nuance in the LEAVES — blossom + colour change; the ground is not everything.
steps.decision: Pivot to daytime, canopy-first. Foliage masses built from ~40k camera-billboarded leaf-dabs (trees/shrubs/yellow Acer/blossom shrubs, layered), over dark branches. Per-leaf seasonal logic, staggered: spring leaf-out + blossom -> summer green -> autumn colour turn (varied amber/orange/red) + leaf fall -> winter bare branches. Blossom-fall & leaf-fall petal particles. Bright daytime palette, soft post.
steps.learned: Leaf-dab masses + per-leaf seasonal logic is the right model for 'nuance in the leaves' — the patchy staggered autumn turn is the most convincing seasonal frame yet; Acer proves per-mass colour identity. Remaining: composition reads as a bank across a lawn, not enclosing (big trees need to arch overhead/fill top; empty sky+ground); branches faint; daytime canopy now lives apart from the Nocturne ground garden — they must merge into one scene.

steps.title: The Merge (daytime master)
steps.tool: Three.js: canopy leaf-dabs + recursive brown branches + 07d floor strokes + dapple + pollinators + petals, one daytime scene
steps.question: User: daytime is master; organic brown trunks; merge the three (canopy framing first); richer autumn esp. maples.
steps.decision: ONE daytime scene merging canopy(09)+floor(07d)+layers(08). Enclosing framing (overhead+side canopy masses, camera low looking up). Recursive 3D brown branch generator (trunk->sub-branches, tapered, woody) as camera-billboard thick-lines. Maple autumn: per-leaf base+MID+LATE colour stops, staggered green->gold->red, maple gold->scarlet vs others yellow->amber. Floor strokes (daytime greens, dappled) + pollinators + blossom/leaf-fall.
steps.learned: The convergence works — first time it reads as the WHOLE garden, daylight, alive through the year. Recursive brown branches + maple gold->scarlet are the asks landed; autumn-maples is the best frame yet. Remaining: empty mid-ground band between canopy and floor (needs bridging shrubs/climbers); floor plants stay green in autumn (should turn/decline); canopy masses ball-like, trunk lone.

steps.title: Beds, Path & Flies (ground structure)
steps.tool: Three.js: ground-zone shader (lawn/earth/path/patio) + bed-constrained planting + 5-kind varied flies
steps.question: User: need lawn/earth/garden beds with structure + a path; more flowers; more varied flies.
steps.decision: Shared bedEdge(z)/pathC(z) (JS+GLSL, true world coords) carve the floor into mown lawn / earth beds (side borders) / stone path winding up the middle / front patio, each coloured + dappled. Floor strokes generated INSIDE the beds as drifts; sparse lawn grass. Richer 8-colour flower palette across the season, brighter tips. Five fly kinds (bumblebee/honeybee/hoverfly/2 butterflies) with distinct size/colour/speed/motion-mode, ~240.
steps.learned: Ground structure is what makes it read as a DESIGNED garden, not plants on a plane — path leads the eye in, beds home the planting, lawn/earth/stone read distinctly; varied flies add life cheaply. Remaining: floor plants stay green in autumn (unify seasonal clock); path wide/straight; flies could be denser.

steps.title: A Real Plant Palette (+ unified seasonal clock)
steps.tool: Three.js: ~23-species plant library with per-plant lifecycle in the floor shader
steps.question: User: unify the seasonal clock; too many grasses (not a London cottage garden); use the plant list, more realistic replicants.
steps.decision: Replaced generic archetypes with a library of ~23 named London cottage/woodland species (hellebore, brunnera, pulmonaria, epimedium, heuchera[purple], bergenia, fern, solomon's seal, ajuga, foxglove, verbascum, veronicastrum, ammi, agapanthus, nepeta, allium, geranium, hydrangea, lobelia, snowdrop, crocus, daffodil, grass[rare]). Each carries shape/foliage/flower/height + wake/sleep/evergreen/autumn-foliage. Per-plant lifecycle in the shader unifies the clock: plants wake in season, brown to autumn colour, die back (unless evergreen); bulbs pulse. Two new shapes (fern frond, flat umbel); packed scalars into vec4 for the 16-attribute GPU limit; drifts of one species; grass weighted down.
steps.learned: Per-plant lifecycle turns a season CURVE into a garden YEAR: spring bulbs -> flowering border -> autumn die-back IN SYNC with the canopy -> winter bare-bones + evergreen structure + snowdrops. Named palette + distinctive foliage (purple heuchera, big bergenia, ferns) reads as a real London border. Winter showcases the recursive brown branches. Strongest the piece has been. Remaining: flower FORMS still approximate (coloured tip masks, no true foxglove-spike/allium-globe geometry); bulbs/accents could be denser; path wide.

steps.title: Flower Forms & Full Beds
steps.tool: Three.js: per-species floret generator (~16-30k flower-dab instances) + denser planting
steps.question: User: real flower forms + fill the beds in.
steps.decision: Replaced colour tip-masks with a FLORET system: per-species FORMS map drives emitFlorets() laying flower dabs in shape — spike (foxglove/verbascum), globe (allium/agapanthus), umbel (ammi), mophead (hydrangea), head (geranium/hellebore), haze (nepeta/brunnera), bell (solomon's seal), single (bulbs), plume (grass). Florets are instanced billboards fading on each plant's bloom window with a bright centre; foliage strokes now pure green. Filled beds: drifts 170->300, wider borders, FMAX 17k->24k.
steps.learned: Flower FORM is a big realism jump — foxglove reads as a spike of bells, allium as a globe, not a smear; form clusters fade per plant's bloom window so borders change shape through the season; denser drifts look gardened not sparse. Unified clock survived (florets seasonal, beds brown with canopy). Remaining: floral ABUNDANCE could go higher; florets are dabs not petal geometry; path wide.

openThreads: Floral ABUNDANCE — more florets / more of the bed flowering at once; florets are billboard dabs not true petal geometry
Bridge the empty MID-GROUND band between canopy-bottom and the low floor (continuous shrubs/climbers — the photo has no gap)
Soften path (stepping-stones not a wide strip); denser flies; even more continuous bed colour
Refine canopy: masses less ball-like; trunk less lone / branches connect into crown; denser foliage
Build per MODEL.md: ZONES A-D; named woodland-floor species; BULB pulses; HUMAN-trace layer (watering can, cat, patio lights)

TRIAL 07 (synthesis): drive the planting from the Trial 05 substrate — species density field decides WHICH ARCHETYPE grows WHERE — so the brush-stroke garden is genuinely ecological (emergent competition/succession), not a season curve
Make the engine data-driven: load Layer-1 JSON species instead of hardcoded (unlocks Trial 02, the non-garden dataset)
